desert_p08_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_001.text: In the morning shade, the lower exchange looked less like a ruin than a rise of ground that happened to contain three doorways. Gao led them to the northern outcrop, where the cistern panel stood within reach of sound stone. Han came with the collection cans and left the drivers ready to pack. Bao carried the remaining field sets. Du held the standard-plan page beside Yue's exterior sketch. The two images agreed in some places and diverged where later walls had been added.

desert_p08_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_002.text: They would follow the visible building, using the old plan to ask questions rather than to command answers. The roof catchment emerged beneath a thin strip of drift at the ridge's base. It was stone, laid in a shallow slope toward the northern channel. Gao could trace the channel from exposed edges without climbing onto the buried roof. A low raised lip separated it from the east loading apron and the quarry drainage hollow. The ordinary runoff path led away from the cistern inlet, while collected roof water entered through a screened settling pocket. Much of the screen was gone.

desert_p08_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_003.text: The pocket held grit and dry leaves, but no obvious industrial residue or open connection to the salt seep.

desert_p08_004.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p08_004.text: Here is the boundary that matters to the source. The loading floor drains east; the roof catchment drains north through this pocket. They are close enough that a copied plan could join them, but the stone lips still separate them. Let us follow the northern channel to the inlet from this ledge. If it breaks into the ground, we stop calling the source roof water until we see where it goes. Yue, mark the surviving lip exactly. Du, keep the standard plan open. I want to know which parts are original and which we are discovering by looking.

desert_p08_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_005.text: At a narrow notch the channel disappeared beneath an intact capstone and reappeared against the cistern wall. Gao inspected both edges with the sighting glass while the farrier checked the ledge. The capstone bridged a short service recess, not an open salt channel. A maintenance opening had been sealed with a fitted stone plug. The plug sat dry above the highest visible stain. Bao examined the stain's relation to the inlet and asked Gao to check the lower wall for seepage. There was none where they could see.

desert_p08_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_006.text: Their confidence grew through connected observations, each smaller than a claim that the whole ruin was harmless. Du found a carved source diagram beside the plug. It showed the settling pocket, the covered conduit, and an overflow directed away from the storage chamber. The diagram's scale differed from the weighing-hall plan, but its direction fitted the exposed work. He copied it with the weathered portions left blank. Yue drew the old and current roof edges beside it. Rain entering the surviving catchment could explain the present water even after the station closed.

desert_p08_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_007.text: The store did not need a secret underground river. A roof, a sealed chamber, and seasons of occasional rain had done the patient work. The overflow outlet was partly buried, yet its raised throat remained above the gauge line. The farrier cleared only the loose grit at its outer mouth with his rod, avoiding any prying against the masonry. A dry stream of dust fell away. There was no fresh wet path from the loading apron into it. Bao noted the source separation and inspected the collection jar's settled sediment. The gritty material resembled the roof pocket's pale dust.

desert_p08_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_008.text: That resemblance supported the source account without replacing the chemical results. She kept the retained sample sealed, so later examination could compare more than their descriptions. Under the north opening a metal plate listed the cistern's routine cleaning intervals and draw procedure. Its last engraved repair date belonged to the station's final active decade. A pencilled maintenance mark survived behind the protective frame, likely made later. Du could read a year and the initials of a keeper, but not identify the person. Somebody had cared for this store after the official staff left.

desert_p08_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_009.text: Tuo might know the local family if they showed her the letters. The mark explained continued maintenance as a possibility, not a ghostly keeper or an assurance that every recent year received the same care.

desert_p08_010.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p08_010.text: We have a plausible isolated roof source, no visible connection to the salt spill, and yesterday's limited screens within their working limits. I want a fresh sample after the pipe flush before deciding on use. The stagnant tap water is not the whole store. We shall compare the fresh draw with the reference and the retained portion. If they agree within the field checks, we can filter sediment and boil the measured collection. We will keep the treatment separate from raw water.

desert_p08_011.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p08_011.text: I should prefer to do that beside the camp stove, where nobody mistakes a passing jar for a drink.

desert_p08_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_012.text: Han opened the outlet gradually while Gao watched the gauge respond. They measured the new flush in one of the marked cans, noting what had already been taken yesterday. The handle turned stiffly but stopped the flow cleanly when closed. Its thread was sound enough to recap. Bao took the fresh sample, and Yue labelled it before any vessel moved. In clearer water the glass scale looked more ordinary than it had at dusk. It was a device doing a limited job. The estimate above it remained an estimate, while the measured cans gave numbers the caravan could actually enter.

desert_p08_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_013.text: The first two comparisons agreed with the previous draw. Bao worked through the rest while Gao checked the stored reference card. There were enough field sets for the paired samples and controls, with a small reserve left afterwards. The case could not support endless curiosity. Du watched the reactions without suggesting an ancestor's hand in their colours. Han stayed near the collection cans, ready to stop rather than adding water before the decision. Yue found the waiting difficult, then remembered the injured guide's cup shaking under Tuo's hand.

desert_p08_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_014.text: Waiting could be an active part of care even when nothing visible moved. While the samples matured, Gao examined the service opening beside the gauge. It looked into a dry passage separated from the cistern by a thick masonry wall. A vent above it connected with the lower rushing sound they had heard from camp. Sunlight reached only a short distance inside. Beyond that, a flat surface glimmered, perhaps glass or glazed ceramic. Gao stayed outside, using the ordinary sighting glass from the ledge. The service passage's roof was the buried slab travellers could mistake for road.

desert_p08_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_015.text: Its present load already included drift. More cart weight belonged among the report's strongest cautions. Du measured the visible floor edge against the loading-height numerals over the eastern door. The difference placed the weighing hall below the apron, just as the manual described. Freight had once been moved across a raised platform while staff worked beside the balance mechanism under shelter. Calling the upper surface a road had erased that arrangement. Yue imagined a loaded water cart passing directly over the buried room and felt cold despite the warming air. No one had driven there today.

desert_p08_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_016.text: Their chosen ridge and gravel camp had avoided it before they understood why avoidance mattered. The farrier found a newer wheel scrape on the northern approach, ending before the buried apron. Somebody had turned a cart there within the past season. It was not enough to identify the driver or their reason. Gao recorded it as recent use of the sound approach, with no proof of entry. Han said the carriers' last turned-back consignment might have come this far. Its office could compare the mark with their driver's account. The physical evidence now offered a question worth asking in town.

desert_p08_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_017.text: It did not require them to invent a missing freight caravan for the pleasure of discovery. A voice called from the ridge before they finished the sketch. The camp's red flag rose above Crescent House's arch, then lowered and rose again: come back, no emergency haste. Han recognised the agreed interruption signal. They capped the outlet, secured the samples for their remaining reaction time, and returned by the northern path. A camel stood outside the camp, chewing with slow indifference while its rider spoke to the quiet driver. The animal carried its own water skins and a light dispatch bag.

desert_p08_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_018.text: It was the first thing Yue had seen all morning that seemed entirely certain about where its feet belonged. The rider had come from Bitter Wells with letters for Han and the carrier commission. He had heard the quarry's report of the guide rescue from the fast receiving-house messenger, but no personal clinical details. The transport wagon still travelled at its gentler pace. He offered a sealed cooperative letter and a separate note from Han's daughter. Han took the family note first, then looked embarrassed and put it safely inside his coat before opening the business letter.

desert_p08_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_019.text: Bao said nobody needed to apologise for checking home. The rider drank from his own flask while the cook offered him a bowl. The cooperative wanted a preliminary route account before the full report. Its members feared the injured guides' story would reach insurers first and become proof that all their northern consignments had been reckless. The secretary asked Han to keep personal names out of circulation until the guides could make their own statements. That request was sensible. Another paragraph asked that no public route warning be issued before the subscribers agreed its wording. Gao read it twice.

desert_p08_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_020.text: Waiting for every interested office could leave the short-route notice standing through another series of crossings. The two requests belonged to different kinds of caution.

desert_p08_021.speaker: han_xun
desert_p08_021.text: Their families deserve control over personal details. We can answer that without arguing. The hazard is another matter. We have already placed a warning at the stranded cart and sent its position to the quarry. I shall tell the secretary exactly that. We owe the subscribers an accurate report, not a silence that makes their next load easier to insure. Gao, prepare the limited route facts we can sign now. Du, separate the mixed-origin notice from the current shelf condition. I want nobody claiming we have declared every northern road unusable because one dispatch makes an insurer nervous.

desert_p08_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_022.text: Gao looked relieved that he had made the distinction himself. Du began a provisional account with the current date, observed load limits, and sites they had actually reached. The guide names remained in the private rescue record. Yue copied the public approach sketch, leaving out their family's contact address and the patient's treatment. The rider explained that the secretary had argued against the silence paragraph, but two large subscribers insisted it be included. Han said their disagreement could remain in the cooperative minutes; it need not be carried into the basin as a closed mouth beside a damaged route.

desert_p08_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_023.text: Han's daughter wrote that her mother's cough had eased under treatment, and that the shop debts remained manageable if he returned before promising every future journey at a discount. She had added a small drawing of a four-wheeled cart, correcting the old child's picture at last. Han read the note behind the first tank, smiling with an expression Yue saw only when she came to fetch a pencil. He folded it slowly. The business letter had threatened future work. The family note did not make that threat disappear, but it gave him somewhere larger than the threat to stand.

desert_p08_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_024.text: The camel rider asked whether the house below was really an exchange. He had been told Crescent House was an abandoned inn. Du showed him the two-site sketch, and the rider admitted he had repeated the inn story to several travellers. He would correct it at the receiving house. Gao asked him to use the provisional sheet rather than promising a new source of water. The cistern checks were not complete. He agreed, though a water discovery would make a much more exciting message.

desert_p08_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_025.text: Yue watched the camel blink and chew, apparently indifferent to the career advantages of carrying exciting news. Bao read the fresh screens at the camp table with Gao checking labels and controls. The measured markers agreed with yesterday's within the field method's range. Combined with the observed roof isolation, the result supported collecting a limited batch for filtration and boiling. She wrote the source, checks, and treatment requirement on the water page. Raw samples stayed away from cups and food. Han accepted the decision only after hearing it in full.

desert_p08_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_026.text: There was still no added tank water, but the possible source had become a usable plan. The distinction changed the crew's afternoon without requiring anyone to celebrate a lake. The cook inspected the collection vessels and set aside two clean pots for the treated water. He could manage the boiling in batches, measuring fuel and final volume instead of trusting the cistern gauge. The larger pot had a fitted lid; the smaller would receive cooled water away from the raw jars. Bao showed him the clean cloth filter and the transfer sequence.

desert_p08_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_027.text: Yue helped label the vessels with chalk tags that could survive the evening light. The cook said he had never had his ordinary work watched so gravely. Bao replied that he had certainly produced meals deserving investigation. Tuo wanted to know how much they intended to draw. Gao described the gauge estimate and the measurable accessible portion. Du read the emergency-use inscription aloud again, including the doubtful characters. Han said a useful supply should not be emptied merely to buy an extra day of scholarship.

desert_p08_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_028.text: Du objected to that description, then admitted the record-room prospect had been growing larger in his thoughts. The carrier report did not require every page inside. Tuo tapped the folded route sheet against her knee. Future stranded travellers might need the cistern more urgently than this well-supplied crew needed another interesting afternoon.

desert_p08_029.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p08_029.text: We can take a measured part, leave an accessible remainder, and depart tomorrow after the necessary closing observations. That gives us time for treatment today without turning this place into a new long commission. The estimate suggests enough above the tap for a useful reserve. We will watch the gauge while drawing and stop short of its lower band. The actual clean addition will be whatever reaches the storage vessels after losses. Our return plan must use that number. Du, if records are visible safely, copy them.

desert_p08_030.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p08_030.text: If they are not, the next hired inspection can bring people equipped for the rooms.

desert_p08_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_031.text: Han agreed. He proposed a total measured draw of one hundred and ninety litres including the inspection flushes and samples already taken. With treatment losses, they expected about one hundred and sixty usable litres, leaving roughly sixty accessible above the outlet by the checked gauge. The exact addition would be measured after cooling. Returning tomorrow kept their margin stronger than spending another full day inside the old district. Bao supported the earlier departure because Tuo's ankle needed an easier bed and steadier observation. Du nodded last.

desert_p08_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_032.text: He had found a door to old knowledge, and now had to practise leaving some of it closed. The rider watched the debate with interest. His office letter had expected him to find a preliminary map, not people discussing how much water to leave in an abandoned station. Han told him the provisional account would mention a screened roof store under measured use, with no promise of permanent drinking supply. Its public location note would follow the completed observation and treatment record. The rider could carry the warning and the corrected two-site approach now.

desert_p08_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_033.text: That was useful news even without treasure. He accepted the packet, then asked whether the cook's lunch could be classified as a confidential preliminary finding. Lunch loosened the camp's mood. Tuo remained in her chair, ankle raised, and told the rider where the ridge road bent before the quarry. He already knew the southern section but welcomed the current culvert report. His camel needed no caravan water during the brief stop; its travel skins and planned municipal refill belonged to his own journey. The cook gave him one extra portion from the contingency food and entered it without ceremony.

desert_p08_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_034.text: Yue sat beside Gao and looked at the copied approach sheet. Their careful observation would travel faster than their bodies, which made its limits matter even more. Before leaving, the rider asked Han for a private answer to the insurers' question: had the old map caused the guides' accident? Han called Gao over rather than producing a convenient yes or no. She described the mixed-origin directions, poor route marking, and fresh drainage change, with the guides' account clearly attributed. Responsibility required more than that first summary. The rider wrote the distinctions in his dispatch notes.

desert_p08_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_035.text: Du watched, perhaps wishing the answer had been a clean defence of his own edition. It was stronger than a defence because it did not require the damaged ground to choose sides. The camel moved off with an ungainly rise, lifting its rider above the tents. Yue followed it with her eyes until the ridge hid the animal's legs. Han's family note stayed inside his coat. The provisional report went in another person's bag toward offices that might welcome or resent it. Gao returned to the water collection plan.

desert_p08_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_036.text: Their afternoon still contained ordinary work: measured cans, clean cloth, fuel, and patience. None of the letters had changed what needed doing to make a raw cistern draw drinkable. Yue found that steadiness useful after the brief intrusion of distant people making urgent requests from shaded rooms. Du asked to accompany the first collection trip so he could copy the remaining gauge inscription. Han agreed and sent a driver to carry the cans. Yue went with Gao to record draw volumes, while Bao stayed by the treatment pots.

desert_p08_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_037.text: Tuo gave the northern-path reminder from her chair, shorter now because they had actually walked it. The farrier checked the ledge again after morning warming. It remained dry and sound. At the outlet, the dark line waited behind glass. Han opened the cap, and water began entering the marked can with a plain, surprisingly gentle sound. The gauge responded as each measured can filled. Gao stopped the flow well above the lower accessible mark, leaving the estimated reserve they had agreed. Inspection draws and the new collection together reached the one hundred and ninety-litre limit.

desert_p08_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_038.text: Part of that had already been discarded or retained for checks. The raw batch for treatment was smaller, and its clean final volume would be smaller still. Yue wrote each transfer before the can moved. The outlet closed without dripping. Du laid his palm against the cold stone beside the emergency inscription, then took it away as if he had understood something that needed no sentence. From the gauge ledge the dry service opening lay at eye height. A rectangular object stood behind its inner grille, dust-coated but recognisably a glass-fronted case. Several narrow columns showed through the grime.

desert_p08_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_039.text: Du had seen such cases in old station manuals: water levels and loading records protected from the air while still visible to staff. Gao allowed one exterior look before they carried the raw batch away. Yue leaned only far enough to see from sound stone. At the case's lower corner a paper label survived beneath the glass, carrying a name for the road neither current map used. The old road name read Stone Channel Traverse. Du traced the letters through the opening without touching the grille. Neither current sheet used that name.

desert_p08_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_040.text: Gao compared its direction with the source diagram and found the traverse followed the buried channel's higher bank, not the public ridge. The label could explain older descriptions of an approach that seemed to have vanished. It did not prove the buried surface still carried a load. Yue copied the visible words and the glass case's position. The discovery enlarged their questions just as their water decision had deliberately shortened the time available for answering them. Behind the glass a sequence of level marks stood beside dates and small weather signs.

desert_p08_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_041.text: Some ink had faded; other lines remained dark where the case protected them from dust. Du could read the nearest column, describing winter runoff passing below the weighing apron. The record connected water level with freight limits. Gao asked him to copy only what he could see clearly and preserve the column boundaries. A figure moved into the wrong year would make a dangerous kind of evidence. His care slowed the work, and Han called time before the desire for a whole record overtook the task they had agreed.

desert_p08_042.speaker: du_she
desert_p08_042.text: I can finish this nearest column in a few minutes. I cannot finish the room by pretending it is all equally visible. Let me take the column and the heading, then I shall come away. The rest needs somebody with proper access and equipment for old paper. I would like that somebody to include me, which is not a qualification. I am aware of the distinction.

desert_p08_043.speaker: du_she
desert_p08_043.text: Han, if I begin making speeches about duty while reaching through the broken grille, you have permission to remind me that my duty includes bringing the pages I already copied back without dropping them into a drain.

desert_p08_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_044.text: Han said he would exercise that permission with enthusiasm. Du copied the nearest column and stepped back himself. The movement mattered more than the joke. Gao recorded the accessible viewpoint and the features that would require another inspection. They left the case behind its grille, with no pane broken to obtain a page. The cistern cap stayed secure. The lower exchange retained both water and records. Yue wondered whether returning later would feel like discovery or responsibility.

desert_p08_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_045.text: For now the raw batch waited in the two service casks the quarry waterkeeper had loaned them, their clean linings checked by Bao before loading. The casks could each hold ninety litres. Filled for this collection, they carried eighty-five apiece, leaving space beneath the lids and keeping each within the handling plan. Han read their marks while the driver secured the bungs. The caravan's tank book still received no credit. Raw water in a temporary cask was a separate load waiting for treatment. Gao helped check the chosen northern carrying route.

desert_p08_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_046.text: Its ledge allowed four adults around a single cask but not two side by side. They would make two journeys. Yue would go ahead with the light staff and stopping flag, keeping the firm path visible. Bao had authorised use of the stretcher's bare carrying rails after the clean medical canvas was removed. The farrier lashed one cask between them with sound cargo straps and checked its combined weight against the rail rating. The four carriers took their places: Han, Gao, the driver, and the farrier. Du carried the papers and walked beside Yue.

desert_p08_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_047.text: Nobody asked the younger cultivator to make the eighty-five litres weightless. The load belonged to ordinary shoulders working together. When the cask rose, water shifted gently inside; the carriers paused until its movement settled, then began the climb. At the first narrow bend Han's foot slipped on loose gravel. The other three halted before the rail twisted. He set his foot back on exposed rock, breathing harder than his contract voice usually allowed. Gao told him to name the slip rather than hide it in an apologetic noise. He said his left sole had lost grip.

desert_p08_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_048.text: Yue marked the patch with the staff and stood beyond it where the next carrier could see. The group moved again slowly. Their care was not graceful. It brought the cask up the ledge without spilling the water or pretending effort had disappeared. Tuo watched them approach the camp and ordered the empty space beside the treatment stove cleared. She could direct that work from her chair more effectively than any of the carriers could while holding a rail. The cook moved his meal pot; the camp worker shifted a light cloth; the quiet driver placed two level blocks.

desert_p08_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_049.text: They lowered the cask onto them and checked its lid. Bao attached a raw-water tag before anyone opened it. Han flexed his fingers, looked at the ridge behind him, and said the second journey would be improved by not spending the first pretending he was younger. The second cask came more smoothly because the carriers used the lesson from the first. Yue had removed the loose surface gravel at the bend with the staff's broad cap, staying clear of the unsupported edge. The driver checked the footing before stepping.

desert_p08_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_050.text: Du carried the remaining collection jar containing the inspection record's retained sample, kept separate from the raw batch. At camp both casks stood in shade, lids secure. Their borrowed wooden sides smelled faintly of the municipal waterhouse. The loan had seemed like an ordinary convenience at the quarry. It had become the practical limit on how much collection they could move safely. Bao checked the carriers for heat strain before the cook began treating the batch. Gao had a headache that eased after sitting in shade and taking her allocated water. Han's palms were red from the rail grips.

desert_p08_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_051.text: The driver and farrier were tired but well. Their extra portions entered the actual day column; the rest of the crew's quieter work balanced some of the forecast. Yue gave back the staff and washed her hands at the designated basin. She had carried neither cask, yet felt tired from keeping the route visible. Attention could consume a body without providing a heroic weight to explain it. The cook spread his fuel book beside the sacks. Twelve kilograms had gone into the journey's cooking so far, leaving twenty-eight of the original forty.

desert_p08_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_052.text: The treatment batch would receive a measured allowance, reviewed after the first kettle. He chose the close-fitting lid, the metal wind shield, and a stove position where gusts would not steal heat along the ground. Bao prepared the sediment filter above the raw receiving vessel. Gao checked the measuring marks against a known can before trusting the pots. Their small arrangements would decide how much of the collected water became a real return margin. Yue labelled three places with broad chalk cards: raw, heating, and cooled. The cards were plain enough for tired eyes.

desert_p08_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_053.text: Bao kept the sample jars at the opposite end of the table. Tuo approved the layout from her chair and pointed out that the route from the eating shade still passed too near the cooled vessel. The camp worker moved the light screen, guiding people around the treatment area. The camp now looked less elegant but worked better. Du joked that it had acquired districts. Han answered that, for once, the districts had boundaries anyone could understand without consulting an old clerk. The first filtered kettle heated slowly. Sediment remained in the cloth; clear water entered the covered pot below.

desert_p08_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_054.text: Bao watched the procedure until the cook demonstrated it without a missed step, then turned to Tuo's ankle. Gao remained beside the water while Yue recorded the batch size and fuel used. Steam began gathering under the lid before the full boil. The cook waited for the proper stage, held it for the agreed treatment time, and moved the kettle onto a stable cooling block. It was ordinary kitchen work given an unusual consequence, and he performed it with fewer jokes than usual. Han read the provisional route account while the kettle cooled.

desert_p08_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_055.text: The copy contained no promise of a safe loaded road across the buried apron. It identified the lower exchange, the two cairns, and the northern foot approach used for inspection. The cistern note stayed provisional until the actual treated volume was measured. He could see how easily a carrier might shorten those paragraphs to two enticing words: water available. He underlined the date and treatment requirement. Gao asked him to leave the underlying observations intact rather than making her caution sound like a refusal to help. He agreed and restored a sentence he had crossed out for brevity.

desert_p08_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_056.text: Du examined his copied level column beside the source diagram. Several high winter readings coincided with a note closing the loading apron to heavy wagons. The note referred to the Stone Channel Traverse, apparently a route along the buried watercourse. A later entry reopened only the upper ridge. That history could explain why modern maps favoured the ridge while freight stories retained a shorter approach. It could also matter to the present quarry bank failure. Du resisted joining the events across decades without more records.

desert_p08_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_057.text: He wrote possible relation, then placed the exact copied words beneath it where readers could test the suggestion themselves. Gao said the old level column justified a later properly equipped inspection. It did not require this crew to remain another day. Han seemed relieved until Du asked who would fund that inspection. The carriers had hired them for an approach report, not the history of every water limit. Han said insurers might pay if the findings changed future loading decisions.

desert_p08_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_058.text: Tuo suggested the village collective deserved a place in the discussion, because its grass and road had already paid for the quarry's shortcut. The proposed next commission began with people rather than with the glamour of an unopened room. Bao asked them to move the funding debate away from the heating kettle. Hot water did not benefit from being surrounded by gesturing experts. They shifted to the map table, and Yue stayed with the cook. He told her that his mother could have stopped the entire debate with one look over her frying pan.

desert_p08_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_059.text: She was curious whether he feared that look. He said everyone did, including the river. The answer made Yue laugh, then she saw him check the lid with a folded cloth before touching it. A person could tell a joke and remain exact in the same breath. The cooled first batch went into a clean measured vessel. Bao approved its handling, and Gao watched its transfer into the second caravan tank through the covered inlet. The tank had room and a checked lining. Only the cooled amount entered the water book as an addition.

desert_p08_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_060.text: Raw water still in the casks remained outside that total. The cook wrote the fuel cost and adjusted the next batches to the tested pace. Han asked Yue to read the entry aloud. Hearing one modest volume seemed more reassuring than hearing the gauge's larger estimate before anyone had touched a kettle. Late light reached the courtyard as the second batch heated. Tuo's ankle had become easier at rest, though standing still hurt. Bao approved the riding arrangement for the return and kept the guide's walking limited.

desert_p08_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_061.text: The equipment driver brought the cart close enough for Tuo to practise entering from the low side with assistance, on firm gravel. Han checked the handhold; Bao watched the foot. The guide completed the movement without twisting the ankle. She looked annoyed by how pleased everyone seemed. Yue said nothing, knowing relief could become another burden when five people displayed it at once. Du asked Tuo about the old road name. She had heard Stone Channel from her father's generation, always as a warning during wet winters.

desert_p08_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_062.text: The route shortened the distance to the upper valley but crossed ground where water could rise beneath a crust. Her brother's freight company had used another winter section, farther north. She would not join that death to this record merely because both involved old retaining work. Du thanked her for the distinction. Yue listened from the water table and understood how grief could search for a pattern large enough to hold itself. Accuracy sometimes required declining that comfort. Han's daughter had drawn the new cart with four solid wheels and an absurdly large flower painted on its side.

desert_p08_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_063.text: He showed the picture to the drivers, who immediately requested the flower for every company vehicle. The quiet driver wanted hers blue; Long Legs wanted a colour the mules might find embarrassing. Han said paint cost money. The farrier replied that the company already spent plenty on things nobody could admire. Their laughter interrupted the more serious talk without erasing it. Yue saw Han fold the note differently afterwards, keeping the picture exposed when he slid it back inside his coat. Gao took the next batch's timing while Yue rested her writing hand.

desert_p08_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_064.text: The surveyor had recovered from the carrying headache, but she did not resume every task at once. Bao insisted the carriers eat before continuing. They ate beside the shade while the cook managed the kettle, accepting a driver's help with fuel weighing. The work belonged to the crew now, rather than to one expert guarding a miraculous discovery. Yue could see each person's contribution in the arrangement: Tuo's path, Du's caption, Han's casks, Bao's checks, Gao's source inspection, the driver's shoulders, the cook's careful heat. The water left in the cistern troubled Du more after the treatment succeeded.

desert_p08_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_065.text: He imagined a future guide reaching the tap with no charcoal or kettle. Raw water would still need boiling, and the road warning would say so. Leaving a reserve did not remove every future difficulty. Bao said neither did emptying it into their safe tank. The choice could preserve an option without promising a completed rescue to people they could not know. Du accepted that with a slow nod. His old essay had offered the station impossible powers. The present report could be useful while asking the next traveller to bring ordinary necessities.

desert_p08_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_066.text: Yue suggested placing the cistern's location on the public correction sheet only after explaining the northern foot approach and the unsafe loading apron. Tuo said carriers might still try to bring a cart down for water. Gao would mark foot access, current date, and measured draw conditions plainly. Han wanted a larger warning symbol than the printer normally allowed. Du agreed to make it part of the figure instead of a tiny footnote. The map's empty space had become an argument about readers whose habits none of them could control.

desert_p08_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_067.text: They could at least give the hazard room to be seen. As evening approached, the cook reviewed the fuel pace again. Treatment would fit inside the reserved allowance if the wind remained within the shield's working shelter. Another driver took over weighing portions while he prepared supper on the second small burner, using the cooking allotment rather than stealing from the water batches. Yue noticed how fatigue made familiar distinctions easier to blur. She rewrote one smudged chalk card before it could become raw or cooled according to whoever needed it. Bao thanked her briefly.

desert_p08_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_068.text: The girl found that brief thanks more comfortable than praise for a virtue she still had to keep practising. The casks grew lighter as the filtered batch passed through the stove. Their insides would need cleaning before return to the quarry keeper, with the loan record retained until actual handover. Han placed that task beside the return route rather than among completed purchases. The keeper had lent useful things, not donated invisible capacity. Du asked whether every loan survived this much writing. Han said the ones that did usually survived the road too.

desert_p08_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_069.text: Yue smiled, but thought of the cloth returned to Tuo after years. Some borrowed objects waited on accounts much less tidy than a cask receipt. Gao called Du over to examine a faint mark in the level-column copy. It resembled the same scale sign missing from the subscriber caption. Here it stood beside a seasonal restriction, distinguishing the loading apron from the upper station's public approach. The repeated sign supported their site identification. It did not name the people responsible for a later dispatch. Du copied the relation onto the corrected sheet and looked almost boyishly pleased.

desert_p08_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_070.text: A small mark restored to its proper company could undo a large confusion. Yue remembered the yard's duplicate harness number and saw the same kind of error at a much older scale. A tiny crooked wing stood below the copied heading. Gao's expression sharpened. She used that same bird beside difficult readings, a habit Du had taught her before her field licence. She opened her current book, compared the shapes, then closed it again. When Du asked what had caught her eye, she said she wanted another morning look through the north opening. Her voice was flatter than usual.

desert_p08_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_071.text: Yue watched her fold the copy with exceptional care, leaving its margin visible. The camp's noise softened as people settled after supper. Tuo's staff lay beside her riding cushion. Bao covered the screened sample jars; Gao stored the original tracing dry; Han counted the return claims without announcing their sum. The cook kept the water heating. Yue sat at the table and wrote the lower building's new place in the story of the road. She crossed out found beneath the salt because the structure had never been wholly lost to everyone. People had seen its openings for years.

desert_p08_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_072.text: What their crew had found was a way to understand its parts together. That distinction mattered to Tuo, who read the line over Yue's shoulder from her chair. She said local people were often introduced to their own ground as witnesses of a stranger's discovery. Gao heard and asked Yue to preserve the guide's wording in the report's source note. Han agreed that the collective's older channel knowledge belonged beside the survey observations. Du put his name after Tuo's on the location description. The order would not settle every question of credit, but it was a concrete choice.

desert_p08_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_073.text: Yue rewrote the sentence, allowing the old station to remain known before it became newly measured. Beyond the tents the buried loading roof held the last light. It looked placid, almost inviting, from this distance. Yue could now imagine the weighing hall beneath it, the dry service passage, the separate cistern, and the level record behind glass. She had not entered any of them. The knowledge came through viewpoints, old diagrams, living memories, and measured water. It felt less complete than a heroic descent would have sounded, and more dependable.

desert_p08_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_074.text: The building remained partly hidden, naturally, under what wind had carried. Tomorrow they would leave much of that hidden work for another properly prepared journey. The next cooled batch entered the tank while the sky darkened. Gao marked its actual volume; Han checked the addition against the receiving can; Bao made sure the raw transfer cloth never touched the clean inlet. The cook used his allotted fuel and shut the stove vent between batches. Yue watched the dark water surface settle under the tank's cover. It carried none of the glass gauge's drama now.

desert_p08_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_075.text: It would become cups, soup, mule troughs, and the weight of a safer return. Those ordinary uses were the reason the ruined station mattered beyond the pleasure of finding it. Before the last batch, the wind changed. The upper house stopped singing, and the lower exchange's rushing note rose sharply across the camp. A cool thread of air moved through the north grille. Gao looked toward the case opening, then at Du's copied level column. He pointed to a weather sign beside one old surge reading: wind turning from the basin before water rose in the buried channel.

desert_p08_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p08_076.text: The present note alone proved no surge. It did give them a reason to check the sky and the return approach while the cook finished the water. Yue took the red flag from its case.
